'''''Trichocentrum carthagenense''''', also known as the '''Coot Bay dancing lady orchid''', is a species of [[orchid]] found from the [[Everglades]], the Caribbean and Mexico, Central America and down to northern Brazil.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cetzal-Ix |first1=William |last2=Carnevali |first2=Germán |last3=Romero-González |first3=Gustavo |title=SYNOPSIS OF THE ''TRICHOCENTRUM''-CLADE (ORCHIDACEAE, ONCIDIINAE) |date=2016 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/90000319 |journal=Harvard Papers in Botany |volume=21 |issue=2 |pages=141–169 |doi=10.3100/hpib.v21iss2.2016.n3 |jstor=90000319 |s2cid=90477190 |issn=1043-4534|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The species name refers to the [[Cartagena, Colombia]], where it was first collected in 1760.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hammer |first=Roger L. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-S0aBgAAQBAJ |title=Everglades Wildflowers: A Field Guide to Wildflowers of the Historic Everglades, including Big Cypress, Corkscrew, and Fakahatchee Swamps |date=2015-01-06 |publisher=Rowman & Littlefield |isbn=978-1-4930-1459-0 |pages=77 |language=en}}</ref>
